findings.description: The install-time Step 6 (Install the gstack-to-plans glue skill) instructs a direct global copy through a raw tilde path -- "If global: copy to `~/.claude/skills/gstack-to-plans/SKILL.md`." -- instead of the <profile> placeholder that Step 1 defines and requires ("<profile> is %USERPROFILE% on Windows. Not HOME, and never ~", SKILL.md:91). The same document explains why this matters: "On a domain machine HOME can point at a redirected network drive while the real profile stays on C: ... That has happened on a machine this stack is developed on" (SKILL.md:92-96), which matches the exact defect class the repo own history already caught once (controller checkout commit 3557bfa: gate: phase-2 PASSED (attempt 2) -- caught + fixed wrong-HOME global deploy). A second occurrence is the uninstall flow Step U7, which checks and deletes global components via raw ~/.claude/ rather than the resolved profile (SKILL.md:527, 529-530, 534, 541, 544, 562-564). Searching the whole file, <profile> notation appears only in Step 1 (lines 82-91); Steps 6 and U7 -- both agent-executed actions, not user-run terminal commands like the explicitly-carved-out Step R2 -- revert to literal tilde paths. This directly contradicts the plan stated success criterion (No global path in the installer resolves through ~ or HOME) and is not covered by any test in tests/packaging/ (the idempotency suite deliberately never exercises global-scope install/uninstall, per its own hard rule against touching the live profile).
findings.evidence: Quoted text from .claude/skills/setup-with-claude/SKILL.md lines 91, 268, 527-544, 562-564, read directly in the aaw-packaging-repair worktree; cross-checked commit 3557bfa in the controller checkout (git log --oneline shows gate: phase-2 PASSED (attempt 2) -- caught + fixed wrong-HOME global deploy) showing this exact bug class recurring after being fixed once already; grep -n <profile> on SKILL.md returns only lines 82-91, confirming Steps 6 and U7 never use the required placeholder.

findings.description: Plan success criterion (The upstream suite passes, with the exact command and exit code recorded) is not literally met: bun run test:windows on the sync branch exits 1 with 7 failing tests. This is not scored as a critical code-quality defect because (a) the phase plan own Risk Assessment table anticipated exactly this outcome -- The upstream gstack suite does not run on native Windows... Record the failure honestly as a platform limitation; do not claim a passing suite that was not run -- and the loop did exactly that; (b) every one of the 7 failures was individually re-run in isolation and attributed to environment (missing jq, Windows Developer Mode off, a Git Bash fork() flake, one load-induced flake) or to a genuine pre-existing upstream bug (browse/test/build.test.ts:16, an unquoted execSync interpolation), none to the sync itself; and (c) the branch carries an empty net tree patch from the merge base, so there is structurally no fork-specific code the sync could have broken.
findings.evidence: Independently re-verified in C:/Users/mharvey2/Coding/gstack-fork: git rev-parse upstream/main and git rev-parse sync/upstream-2026-08-26 both return ad8400543cd9ce8d07641362db48d44a95417e33 (identical); git diff --stat 029356e1f0693f22cb1fa4524c9b0f28ceab5a1b origin/main returns empty (empty net patch, exit 0, no output); git rev-list --left-right --count upstream/main...origin/main returns 89 and 3; browse/test/build.test.ts:16 read directly in the sync worktree confirms execSync with an unquoted SERVER_NODE interpolation, matching the reported bug exactly; command -v jq on this machine exits 1 (absent), matching the attribution.

findings.description: The plan Explicitly NOT included scope states Pushing anything. Every branch in this phase stays local until the external-write gate, yet both feat/aaw-packaging-repair and docs/herdr-v0.2-import were pushed to origin during this phase, per the loop-003 evidence record (Pushed: yes, on 2026-08-26, under the loop-003-5 human gate). Independently confirmed the push actually happened. This is recorded as an out-of-primary-scope process observation for the record, not a code-quality defect: the evidence frames it as a deliberate, disclosed decision made under an explicit human gate, and it is for the orchestrating process (not this code-quality review) to judge whether that gate satisfied the external-write gate the plan refers to.
findings.evidence: git ls-remote origin refs/heads/feat/aaw-packaging-repair in the aaw-packaging-repair worktree returns 360ab3c3af1d47d9e6cb495f9042a470cb7f29ae for refs/heads/feat/aaw-packaging-repair, matching git rev-parse HEAD exactly -- the branch is genuinely on origin, not merely claimed.

findings.description: No project-root CLAUDE.md is present or accessible in either the controller checkout or the aaw-packaging-repair worktree (it is deliberately gitignored per the .gitignore own comment: Local agent briefing (not public)), so this review could not check the phase Python/shell style against an authoritative project-specific convention document. Observed instead, without a confirmed convention to check against: the tests/packaging/*.sh scripts use a bash shebang with bash-specific constructs (arrays, mktemp -d, double bracket tests) rather than POSIX sh; the four Python modules (.aaw/detect.py, tools/aaw-audit.py, tests/packaging/project_ops.py, tests/packaging/validate-manifest.py) have extensive module and function docstrings but largely omit explicit parameter and return type annotations on function signatures (e.g. def user_profile(env=None) at .aaw/detect.py:50). Recorded as info only since no CLAUDE.md was found to confirm these are violated conventions for this project.
findings.evidence: ls CLAUDE.md fails with No such file or directory in both the aaw-packaging-repair worktree and the Advanced-AI-Workflows controller checkout; the .gitignore comment above the CLAUDE.md exclusion line confirms it is an intentionally untracked local file, not merely missing from this checkout.

findings.description: Three caveats already disclosed by loops 002/003 and their cross-model reviewer were independently confirmed accurate rather than newly discovered: (1) the restored glue skill contains zero AskUserQuestion callouts although phase 1 accepted it on the basis of three such callouts; (2) the fresh-clone doc-scan still cannot match a documented install source with no file extension at all; (3) tests/packaging/documented-destinations.txt is an exception allowlist whose reason convention is not parser-enforced. All three are pre-existing, honestly disclosed in the evidence/README/SETUP, and already tracked as open follow-up work rather than undisclosed defects from this phase.
findings.evidence: grep -c AskUserQuestion on the glue skill returns 0 in the aaw-packaging-repair worktree, confirming the disclosed gap; tests/packaging/documented-destinations.txt read directly shows the file has no real entries by design, matching the disclosed caveat text.

failure_notes: Critical finding: .claude/skills/setup-with-claude/SKILL.md Steps 6 and U7 still instruct global-scope actions through raw tilde-based paths rather than the <profile> (percent USERPROFILE percent) resolution Step 1 of the same file mandates and the plan success criteria require (No global path in the installer resolves through ~ or HOME). This reintroduces, in newly-authored phase-4 content, the same defect class the programme own history already caught and fixed once (controller commit 3557bfa: caught + fixed wrong-HOME global deploy). Recommended fix: rewrite Step 6 global-copy instruction and Step U7 global-check and removal instructions to resolve and use <profile> exactly as Step 1 does, then re-run the gate.
